met_analysis:
The Depression over Jharkhand moved west-northwestwards and weakened into a well marked low pressure area over the same region at 1730 hrs IST of today, the 14th August, 2026. It is likely to move slowly west- northwestwards and weaken further into a low pressure area over the same region during next 12 hours.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Firozpur, Rohtak, Hamirpur, Sidhi, centre of well marked low pressure area over Jharkhand, Digha & thence southeastwards to Eastcentral Bay of Bengal.
The Shear Zone now runs roughly along Lat. 22°N across central & adjoining north Peninsular India between 4.5 & 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southwards with height.
The Western Disturbance now seen as a cyclonic circulation over Central Pakistan with a trough aloft in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southwest Rajasthan adjoining Pakistan between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level has merged with the above system.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northwest Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhoodat 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The north-south trough from northwest Rajasthan to northeast Arabian sea across Gujarat at 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over northwest Bay of Bengal between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea level.
